item.title: Danish business leaders see opportunities in China's 15th Five-Year Plan
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-13
Panelists take part in a discussion during a dialogue on China-Denmark relations in Klampenborg, Denmark, Nov. 11, 2026. (Photo by Liu Zhichao/Xinhua) COPENHAGEN, Nov. 12 (Xinhua) -- Danish business leaders and former diplomats have said that China's 15th Five-Year Plan could open up new opportunities for economic cooperation between Denmark and China in areas such as wind power, pharmaceuticals and green shipping. They made these remarks at panel discussions on China's latest five-year blueprint and the China-Denmark relations in Klampenborg, Denmark, on Wednesday. Former Danish Ambassador to China Friis Arne Petersen said the plan covered a wide range of industries where the two countries could work together if policy conditions allowed. Petersen said China's push to develop new quality productive forces, including through advances in artificial intelligence, could shape future cooperation in industry, agriculture, environmental protection and energy. He pointed to pharmaceuticals as an area where Danish companies could work with Chinese partners on research, manufacturing and sales. Ove Ullerup, a former Danish diplomat and chairman of the board of Asia House, an association which works to strengthen ties between Denmark and Asia, said China's green transition targets could open up new areas of cooperation with Denmark. He noted that the two countries established a comprehensive strategic partnership in 2008 and launched a joint green work program in 2023. Peter Dige Thagesen, head of geopolitics at the Confederation of Danish Industry, said Denmark's strengths in wind power, electricity and green technology align with China's priorities, and cooperation opportunities also exist in life sciences, food production and green shipping. Thagesen said a survey of the confederation's members showed that Danish companies wanted to maintain trade with China while reducing dependence in critical areas. Hans Henrik Pontoppidan, secretary-general of the Danish-Chinese Business Forum, said Danish companies should consider new ways to work with Chinese partners on research and development, particularly in health care. Chinese Ambassador to Denmark Wang Xuefeng said the five-year blueprint has highlighted advances in science and technology, the green transition and further opening up, which would create more opportunities for Denmark and other partners. The event was jointly organized by the Chinese Embassy in Denmark, the Danish-Chinese Business Forum and Asia House. ■ Attendees listen to remarks during a dialogue on China-Denmark relations in Klampenborg, Denmark, Nov. 11, 2026. (Photo by Liu Zhichao/Xinhua)

item.title: China-Africa photo exhibition deepens friendship, cultural ties
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-13
Guests visit the China-Africa Impressions Photography Exhibition in Addis Ababa, the capital of Ethiopia, Nov. 12, 2026. China-Africa Impressions Photography Exhibition opened Thursday here showcasing cultural ties, people-to-people exchanges and time-honored friendship between China and Africa. Held at the United Nations Economic Commission for Africa (UNECA), the photography exhibition featured 64 photographs, which were selected from 283 entries submitted by 151 photographers of 26 nationalities. (Xinhua/Geng Xinning) ADDIS ABABA, Nov. 12 (Xinhua) -- China-Africa Impressions Photography Exhibition opened Thursday in Addis Ababa, the capital of Ethiopia, showcasing cultural ties, people-to-people exchanges and time-honored friendship between China and Africa. Held at the United Nations Economic Commission for Africa (UNECA), the photography exhibition featured 64 photographs, which were selected from 283 entries submitted by 151 photographers of 26 nationalities. The photographs were captured in more than 30 African countries and China. 24 of them won awards for uniquely depicting the diversity of China and Africa, demonstrating their development, achievements, rich cultural heritage, wildlife and landscapes. Opening the exhibition, Jiang Feng, head of the Chinese Mission to the African Union, said the photography exhibition is a vivid example of China-Africa joint efforts to implement the Global Civilization Initiative that calls for respect for the diversity of civilizations, stronger international people-to-people exchanges, and inclusive coexistence and mutual learning. "The exhibition provides an opportunity to further deepen mutual understanding and friendship between the peoples of China and Africa, enable exchanges among civilizations to transcend barriers, and bring our peoples closer across mountains and seas, thus laying a stronger and more enduring foundation of public support for China-Africa friendship," Jiang said. Noting that the China-Africa friendship has a long history and has grown stronger over time, Jiang hopes that the exhibition will open new opportunities to enhance mutual understanding between the peoples of China and Africa, deepen their cultural exchanges and help build an all-weather China-Africa community with a shared future. Mama Keita, deputy executive secretary for programme support at the UNECA, said the photographs showcase everyday moments, bringing together places, cultures and perspectives in a shared visual dialogue, honoring both distinctiveness and common humanity. "I hope these photographs will inspire conversation, broaden our perspectives and encourage us to see our diverse cultures, experiences and heritage with fresh eyes while discovering the common ground that connects China and Africa," she said. The event, co-organized by the Chinese Mission to the African Union and the UNECA, attracted nearly 200 guests. It also came as the two sides celebrate the China-Africa Year of People-to-People Exchanges. "As we celebrate the China-Africa Year of People-to-People Exchanges, we are reminded that connections between countries are built not only through meetings and agreements, but also through people, curiosity, shared experiences, cultural exchanges and the stories we tell one another," Wubshet Tolosa, representative of award-winning photographers, said during the event. ■ Jiang Feng, head of the Chinese Mission to the African Union, speaks during the opening ceremony of the China-Africa Impressions Photography Exhibition in Addis Ababa, the capital of Ethiopia, Nov. 12, 2026. item.title: COP31 participants say China injects impetus into global green development
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-13
ANTALYA, Türkiye, Nov. 12 (Xinhua) -- During the ongoing 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31), officials and representatives from governments and international organizations have praised China's commitment to green transition, saying it has injected impetus into global green development. They made the comments following the release of the English version of a report at COP31 China Pavilion on Tuesday. The report, titled "Lucid Waters and Lush Mountains Are Invaluable Assets -- China's Path to Green Development," aims to provide the international community with a comprehensive understanding of China's vision for green development, its practical implementation and its global significance. It was jointly compiled by a research team from the Research Center for Xi Jinping Thought on Ecological Civilization, the Xinhua Institute, and the Development Research Center of China's National Forestry and Grassland Administration. The concept of China's Ecological Civilization fundamentally demonstrates that "economic development and environmental protection do not need to compete, but should instead work together," Stewart Maginnis, deputy director general of the International Union for Conservation of Nature, said in an interview with Xinhua in the Turkish coastal city of Antalya, the host city of COP31. He commended China's real commitment to protecting, conserving and restoring ecosystems, emphasizing that natural resources are viewed under China's green vision not just for their environmental value, but also as part of the country's development framework. UN Climate Change Executive Secretary Simon Stiell described China's energy transition as "nowhere else on Earth," saying it has spurred innovation and lowered costs around the globe. International Energy Agency Executive Director Fatih Birol said at the conference that China has made major achievements in electric vehicles, renewable energy and battery storage, adding that "China has shown the world the way." Attending the launch event of the report, Tennant Reed, director of climate change and energy at Australian Industry Group, welcomed the launch of the document, saying it could better explain China's green development experience. Having visited China multiple times for travel and academic seminars, Reed told Xinhua that he was deeply impressed by the country's green transition achievements. "There have been really remarkable improvements in some key issues, including urban air quality," Reed said. It is very encouraging that the country is setting national policy instruments and supporting the growth of green power sources for industry and households, he added. Noting that this progress is not only vital for China itself but also for the global response to climate change, Reed said China has become a primary source of clean energy, low-emission and zero-emission technologies, and the country's experience and expertise offer valuable tools and reference for other nations to meet their emission targets. Australian Minister for Climate Change and Energy Chris Bowen, who serves as COP31 president of negotiations, said China's clean energy investments are driving down battery and solar costs worldwide. "That benefits China's own economic development, and it benefits the rest of the world as well," he said. The COP31, which will run until Nov. 20, brings together international delegates, climate experts and stakeholders to accelerate global climate action, enhance green cooperation and advance the implementation of the Paris Agreement.■

item.title: EPC summit brings Europe together, but delivers few concrete results
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-13
European Council President Antonio Costa, Irish Prime Minister Micheal Martin and Swiss President Guy Parmelin (from L to R) attend a press conference following the ninth European Political Community (EPC) summit in Dublin, Ireland, Nov. 12, 2026. The summit is co-chaired by Irish Prime Minister Micheal Martin and European Council President Antonio Costa, under the theme "Europe -- strong, secure and connected." (Xinhua/Li Mangmang) DUBLIN, Nov. 12 (Xinhua) -- The ninth European Political Community (EPC) summit concluded in Dublin on Thursday, bringing together around 50 leaders from across Europe and beyond, with Ukraine, European security and economic competitiveness topping the agenda. The summit offered European leaders a platform to exchange views amid mounting geopolitical uncertainty. Yet behind the show of diplomatic unity, the gathering exposed a familiar weakness: Europe's determination to shape its own future is not yet matched by its ability to deliver concrete results. A BROAD GATHERING Held at the Convention Centre Dublin, the summit was the largest gathering of heads of state and government ever hosted by Ireland, prompting the country's biggest-ever policing and security operation. Among its notable features was the participation of leaders from outside the European Union (EU), including British Prime Minister Andy Burnham and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney. Carney attended as a guest, underscoring Canada's efforts to deepen its partnership with Europe. Burnham, meanwhile, used the gathering to strengthen ties with European partners ahead of another EU-Britain summit scheduled for Nov. 20. The presence of Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky also attracted considerable attention, particularly as the gathering coincided with renewed U.S.-mediated diplomatic efforts to end the Ukraine conflict. The EPC's informal format also allowed leaders to hold bilateral and small-group meetings, offering opportunities for exchanges that are often harder to arrange within the more structured framework of EU summits. UKRAINE AND SECURITY DOMINATE DISCUSSIONS Ukraine dominated the discussions, with European leaders pressing for a greater role in negotiations over the conflict and the continent's future security arrangements. Addressing the summit, Zelensky described recent negotiations in Abu Dhabi as "serious, not empty," pointing to an agreement on a prisoner-of-war exchange. However, he questioned why Washington and Moscow were discussing a new security framework for Europe without direct European participation. "We need to make sure that Europe becomes a regular part of these negotiations," he said. European Council President Antonio Costa also stressed that Europe's security could not be decided without European involvement, calling for a ceasefire and progress towards a lasting peace agreement. French President Emmanuel Macron said that around 40 European countries had agreed on "common principles for Europe's future security," stressing the need for closer coordination across the continent. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen also announced that the EU was preparing its 22nd sanctions package against Russia, alongside a proposal to address Ukraine's financial needs in 2027. At the closing press conference, Irish Prime Minister Micheal Martin identified four main outcomes of the discussions: continued support for Ukraine, closer cooperation against hybrid threats, greater use of technological innovation and efforts to provide cleaner and more affordable energy. However, the meeting produced few concrete measures on these broader challenges, with leaders largely reiterating existing priorities and commitments. A FORUM STRUGGLING TO PROVE ITS VALUE The Dublin gathering also brought renewed scrutiny of the EPC itself, with questions growing over whether the forum has become more symbolic than substantive. Launched in 2022 at Macron's initiative, the EPC was designed as a platform for political dialogue among European countries, regardless of whether they belong to the EU. Unlike formal EU institutions, however, it has no permanent decision-making structure and cannot adopt binding decisions. Its summits typically end without a collective final communique. That flexibility allows leaders to meet and exchange views without the constraints of formal negotiations. But it also leaves the forum with a fundamental challenge: demonstrating what it can achieve beyond bringing political leaders into the same room. On Thursday, Politico reported that some European diplomats and officials had grown frustrated with the EPC, viewing it as another gathering that produces limited practical results. According to the report, one diplomat expressed hope that the forum would not survive Macron's departure from office in 2027, while others questioned the need for yet another high-level meeting on Europe's increasingly crowded diplomatic calendar. The French presidency rejected such criticism, arguing that the EPC had become an important diplomatic platform. Future summits have already been scheduled through 2028, including meetings in Switzerland and Greece. Beyond questions about the EPC's future, the Dublin summit highlighted a broader dilemma facing European diplomacy: while leaders insist that Europe must have a stronger voice in shaping the outcome of the Ukraine conflict, they have yet to agree on who should speak for the continent at the negotiating table. ■ European Council President Antonio Costa attends a press conference following the ninth European Political Community (EPC) summit in Dublin, Ireland, Nov. 12, 2026. item.title: Budapest conference highlights RMB's growing role in trade, financing
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-13
Guests attend a panel discussion during the 10th Budapest Renminbi Initiative Conference in Budapest, Hungary, on Nov. 12, 2026. Themed "The Role of Renminbi in the International Monetary System," the conference was jointly organized by Hungary's central bank and Bank of China CEE Ltd. The annual forum is part of the Budapest Renminbi Initiative, launched by the central bank in 2015 to promote RMB use in Hungary and strengthen financial ties with China. (Xinhua/Hu Zhixuan) BUDAPEST, Nov. 12 (Xinhua) -- The renminbi (RMB) is broadening financing options for banks and businesses engaged in trade and investment between China and Central and Eastern Europe (CEE), participants said Thursday at the 10th Budapest Renminbi Initiative Conference. Themed "The Role of Renminbi in the International Monetary System," the conference was jointly organized by Hungary's central bank and Bank of China CEE Ltd. The annual forum is part of the Budapest Renminbi Initiative, launched by the central bank in 2015 to promote RMB use in Hungary and strengthen financial ties with China. Hungarian central bank Governor Mihaly Varga said the global financial system was becoming more multipolar, with regional financial networks gaining importance. Cross-border RMB receipts and payments totaled 70.6 trillion yuan (10.57 trillion U.S. dollars) in 2025, up 10.1 percent year-on-year, according to the People's Bank of China. "There is no doubt that the RMB will play a very important role in the world economy of the future," Varga said. In an interview with Xinhua, central bank Deputy Governor Daniel Palotai said the initiative aimed to facilitate wider RMB use in financial transactions as more Chinese companies and banks operated in Hungary. "Hungary wants to serve as a bridge between the East and the West in this regard," Palotai said. Chinese battery maker CATL and electric vehicle manufacturer BYD are among the companies investing in Hungary. Chinese companies' planned and implemented investment projects in Hungary were worth more than 26 billion euros (28.8 billion dollars), with over 30,000 jobs created, according to Chinese Ambassador to Hungary Gong Tao. Gong also highlighted financial cooperation projects, including the launch of Central and Eastern Europe's first RMB clearing bank in Hungary in 2015 and Hungary's cumulative issuance of 11 billion yuan (1.65 billion dollars) in sovereign panda bonds. Laszlo Bencsik, deputy CEO and chief strategic and financial officer of Hungary's OTP Bank, said the bank had raised 3.5 billion yuan (525 million dollars) through agreements with major Chinese banks and a dim sum bond issuance over the past few years, helping diversify its funding sources. He said companies earning RMB revenues from exports to China could borrow in the same currency to hedge currency risks. "It has to come as a natural demand from clients," Bencsik said. Yu Wenjian, head of the Shanghai Head Office of the People's Bank of China, said RMB use was expanding beyond trade settlement to financing, investment, pricing and reserves. China would further open its financial markets and improve cross-border payment services, he said. "As Chinese companies go global, the RMB needs to go global too," Wang Huiyao, founder and president of the Center for China and Globalization, told Xinhua, calling for more RMB investment products and accessible financial services for smaller businesses. "International financial cooperation is built over time. It needs consistency and mutual confidence," Palotai said in his closing remarks, expressing hope that the discussions would lead to further cooperation in the years ahead. ■ The 10th Budapest Renminbi Initiative Conference is held in Budapest, Hungary, on Nov. 12, 2026. item.title: Xi to attend APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting, related events in Shenzhen
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-13
BEIJING, Nov. 13 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping will chair the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting and deliver remarks, a Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson announced Friday. The meeting will be held in Shenzhen from Nov. 18 to 19 under the theme "Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together," the spokesperson said. The APEC CEO Summit will be held in Shenzhen from Nov. 17 to 18 under the theme "To Prosper and Win the Future Together," the spokesperson said, adding that President Xi will attend the opening ceremony and deliver a keynote speech. President Xi will hold a welcome banquet for participating leaders and representatives, and hold bilateral meetings with foreign leaders on the sidelines of the meeting, the spokesperson added. ■

item.title: Macao holds photo exhibition to mark 160th birth anniversary of Sun Yat-sen
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-12
Macao Special Administrative Region (SAR) Chief Executive Sam Hou Fai addresses the opening ceremony of a photo exhibition commemorating the 160th anniversary of Sun Yat-sen's birth in Macao, south China, Nov. 12, 2026. A photo exhibition commemorating the 160th anniversary of Sun Yat-sen's birth opened in China's Macao SAR on Thursday. (Xinhua/Cheong Kam Ka) MACAO, Nov. 12 (Xinhua) -- A photo exhibition commemorating the 160th anniversary of Sun Yat-sen's birth opened in China's Macao Special Administrative Region (SAR) on Thursday. The exhibition recounts the legendary life of Sun, one of the nation's revered revolutionary forefathers, with over 100 pieces of historical artifacts and photographs, audio recordings and documentaries. Addressing the opening ceremony, Macao SAR Chief Executive Sam Hou Fai noted that Macao shares a profound and special historical bond with Sun. Macao is where he began his mission to do good for the nation and the people, said Sam. Macao is also a cradle of Sun's revolutionary cause, a safe haven in times of crisis as well as a spiritual home where he cherished family affection, said Sam, adding that the best way to commemorate Sun is to carry forward his noble spirit and strive for national rejuvenation. One of the five chapters of the exhibition was dedicated to Sun's career beginning at Macao's Kiang Wu Hospital as a doctor known for seeing patients for free. Wong Kit Cheng, a nurse at the hospital and a member of the Legislative Assembly of the Macao SAR, told Xinhua that she views Sun as her role model and will continue to serve the public by pursuing the mission to cure. The photo exhibition will run through Nov. 27. The Macao SAR also scheduled other events including seminars, themed city tours and the issuance of commemorative stamps. ■ A visitor views exhibits at a photo exhibition commemorating the 160th anniversary of Sun Yat-sen's birth in Macao, south China, Nov. 12, 2026. item.title: Technology reshapes China's agricultural modernization
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-12
* China's autumn grain harvest has withstood the test of disasters this year, with more than 90 percent of the crop gathered by early November and full-year output expected to exceed 700 million tonnes for a third consecutive year. * Technology has carried more of the load. Recent years have seen sustained efforts to raise per-unit yields through integrating improved farmland, seed, machinery and methods, with techniques such as rational close planting, precision sowing and integrated water-fertilizer irrigation. * More than 95 percent of villages have 5G coverage, rural internet penetration has reached 69.5 percent, and the share of farming guided by digital information is rising about 2 percentage points a year in China. BEIJING, Nov. 12 (Xinhua) -- China's autumn grain harvest has withstood the test of disasters this year, with more than 90 percent of the crop gathered by early November and full-year output expected to exceed 700 million tonnes for a third consecutive year. That was the assessment delivered on the latest episode of China Economic Roundtable, an all-media talk show hosted by Xinhua News Agency, where guests discussed how technology is changing not just how much China farms, but how it farms. HARVESTS WITHSTANDING DISASTERS "Nationwide, autumn grain production has withstood the test of disasters, the overall situation is fairly good, and the foundation for a good harvest is solid," said Zhao Changbao, director of the Rural Economy Research Center of the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs. The approach to disasters has shifted, he noted. Rather than responding after damage occurs, agricultural departments moved work ahead of the weather, organizing a 100-day campaign to strengthen field management and combat disasters, and holding regular consultations with meteorological, water resources and emergency management authorities. Technology has carried more of the load. Recent years have seen sustained efforts to raise per-unit yields through integrating improved farmland, seed, machinery and methods, with techniques such as rational close planting, precision sowing and integrated water-fertilizer irrigation. Northeast China's Heilongjiang Province, the country's largest grain producer, has maintained output above 80 million tonnes for two successive years and expects a record harvest this year, said Zhu Huasheng, deputy director of the province's agriculture department. This province has developed 125 million mu (about 8.3 million hectares) of high-standard farmland, achieved near-full coverage of improved seed, and reached a mechanization rate of 99.34 percent for ploughing, sowing and harvesting, with 88,000 new types of agricultural business entities bringing smallholders into the effort. In Dongjiao Village, in the central Chinese province of Hubei, meanwhile, where villagers once suffered from acute drought, ponds and embankments have improved water management efforts, while a heat-tolerant, lodging-resistant rice variety yielded more than 13.5 tonnes per hectare this year, said Hu Aiguo, Party secretary of the village. Mechanization and specialized services have also helped cut losses. In north China's Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, more than 19,000 farm machines and 1,710 service providers were deployed for the autumn harvest this year. "Agricultural production is shifting from a single focus on raising field yields to raising yields, cutting losses and improving quality at the same time," Zhao said. SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY AS SUPPORT The change starts at the seed. In Wuchang, a rice-growing county in Heilongjiang known for its premium rice, a scan of the code on a bag traces where the seed was sown, how the field was managed and when the grain was milled. Local firms have worked with the Chinese Academy of Sciences to purify and rejuvenate Daohuaxiang No. 2, the variety behind Wuchang's reputation, and have built breeding centers, a 333-hectare propagation base and a multiplication base in south China's Hainan Province. Machinery carries this change into the field. China's first tractor rolled off the line in 1958, ending the era of farming behind oxen. First Tractor Company Limited, a leading agricultural machinery provider, now builds 320-450 horsepower tractors with continuously variable transmission, and its Dongfanghong tractors hold straight-line accuracy within 2.5 centimeters using BeiDou positioning. In October, this company, notably, unveiled an onboard AI agent at an agricultural machinery exhibition in north China's Tianjin that advises operators as they work. "Domestic smart machinery makes sowing faster and more precise," said Wang Dongqing, deputy chief engineer of First Tractor. Mechanization, he added, is the link that connects people, machines, land and services. Digital tools are spreading at the same time. "In the past we farmed largely by watching the sky, the land and our experience," Zhao said. "What is changing now is that we are starting to watch data, algorithms and screens." More than 95 percent of villages have 5G coverage, rural internet penetration has reached 69.5 percent, and the share of farming guided by digital information is rising about 2 percentage points a year in China. The country's "No. 1 central document" for 2026 calls for integrating AI with agricultural development, and an action plan for 2026-2030 sets smart farms, intelligent breeding and AI application scenarios as priorities for the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030). "Digital villages and AI are no longer an optional question," Zhao said. "They are a required one for agricultural modernization." In Dongjiao, young people who returned from cities now use smart machinery and sensor networks, and grain growers have formed cooperatives to grow organic rapeseed for premium buyers. "Village development depends on young people putting down roots," Hu said. Zhao stressed wider channels for bringing talent to villages, more concrete services for keeping them, and a thicker foundation for training local farmers. INTEGRATION FOR DEVELOPMENT Technology's effect on incomes is clearest where it meets the market. Heilongjiang has built a provincial brand for black-soil produce and promotes contract farming under which buyers order before planting. "In the past we planted whatever we could and then looked for buyers," Zhu said. "Now we plant what has been ordered." Dongjiao has established 67 hectares each of cropland, peach orchards and fish ponds, and has also developed its rural tourism. Per capita income in the village reached 30,123 yuan (roughly 4,484.32 U.S. dollars) last year. "Goods that used to be sold by the basket at low prices are now sold by the box or by the piece, at several times the old price," Zhao said, crediting livestreaming, e-commerce and branding. Wang said the next five years are both an opportunity and a responsibility for farm machinery makers, and that First Tractor will help rural young people use machinery as a platform for starting businesses. For a country producing around 700 million tonnes of grain a year on a fixed land base, the key, as Zhao put it, is "putting technology into real agricultural production scenarios," as technologies are speeding up the modernization of agriculture and rural areas.■

item.title: Explainer: How the CPC turns clean governance into momentum for capable officials
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-12
BEIJING, Nov. 12 (Xinhua) -- In persevering with full and rigorous self-governance, the Communist Party of China (CPC) highlighted efforts to stimulate Party members' and officials' enthusiasm in tackling challenges. How will the CPC deliver on this commitment? At the fifth plenary session of the 20th CPC Central Committee in October, the CPC leadership sent the signal -- equally important to full and rigorous self-governance is how to encourage Party members and officials to better fulfill their duties, take on new challenges and tackle them. The focus of efforts has been set on creating a clean and enabling political environment. But the drive to stimulate Party members' and officials' enthusiasm doesn't stop here. In an enabling political environment, the next thing they need to better serve the people is competence. Currently, the world is undergoing changes unseen in a century, and China is at a critical moment when the foundation for basically realizing socialist modernization needs to be consolidated and all-out efforts should be made to advance the cause. It is more imperative than ever before to improve the competence of officials. Officials need to develop their abilities to advance high-quality development, serve the people, forestall and defuse risks, and apply law-based thinking and approaches in their work. For this purpose, they are encouraged to work at the primary level, keep abreast of new technologies, new industries and new business models, and learn the latest knowledge and expertise required for the fulfillment of duties. The composition of the CPC membership has changed, with officials born after China's reform and opening-up in 1978 taking up an increasingly large share. The healthy career growth of those officials has been highlighted on the agenda of the CPC's full and rigorous self-governance. The CPC creates opportunities for them to build up their skills and abilities in practice, whether on the front line of reform, development and stability endeavors, in major tasks, or in challenging but key positions. Targeted training programs revolving around social and economic development goals during the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030) have been planned to help young officials close the knowledge gap and shore up their weaknesses in fulfilling duties. The CPC also pledged to unequivocally support and speak up for those who assume responsibility and do solid work, particularly when they encounter setbacks or criticisms because of their bold and proactive moves in performing duties, or when they suffer from injustice because of misunderstanding or false accusations. The original aspiration and mission of the CPC are to seek happiness for the Chinese people, and rejuvenation for the Chinese nation. The CPC understands that the political ideal of serving the people and good governance cannot be achieved if pursuing power for power's sake or personal benefits becomes the ultimate goal of governance. That's why the CPC has been taking a tough stance against corruption particularly since 2012, and why it places such great importance on building a clean political environment and a contingent of capable officials. Governing the Party with strict discipline, the CPC is protecting the level playing field and stimulating positive energy for shouldering responsibilities. In this sense, such a Party self-governance endeavor bolsters economic and social development, and ultimately the wellbeing of the people. ■

item.title: Xi calls for carrying forward Sun Yat-sen's legacy in national rejuvenation drive
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-12
Chinese President Xi Jinping, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, addresses a gathering to commemorate the 160th anniversary of Sun Yat-sen's birth at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 12, 2026. (Xinhua/Yue Yuewei) BEIJING, Nov. 12 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday called for carrying forward the legacy of Sun Yat-sen, one of the nation's revered revolutionary forefathers, to make joint efforts for national rejuvenation and turn into reality the great dream of all Chinese people since the advent of modern times. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks at a gathering held in Beijing to commemorate the 160th anniversary of Sun's birth. Born in 1866, Sun led the Revolution of 1911 more than a century ago to abolish the absolute monarchy that had ruled China for thousands of years. Sun died in 1925. Thursday's gathering in the Great Hall of the People was attended by about 3,000 people, including senior Chinese leaders Li Qiang, Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang and Li Xi, who are members of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee. Wang presided over the event. Xi met with Sun's relatives and representatives of overseas guests before the event started. In his speech, Xi hailed Sun as a great national hero, a great patriot and a great pioneer of China's democratic revolution. He said that Chinese communists are the most steadfast supporters, loyal collaborators, and faithful successors to the revolutionary cause initiated by Sun. For more than 100 years, the CPC has led the Chinese people in writing the most magnificent chapter in the history of the Chinese nation, Xi said. "The best way for us to remember Dr. Sun is to emulate, inherit and carry forward his invaluable spirit, steadily advancing our endeavors to build a great country and rejuvenate our nation," Xi said. Highlighting Sun's lifelong devotion to the country, Xi called on all Chinese people to learn from Sun and promote patriotism to strive for a strong and prosperous China. He also lauded Sun's dedication to the people, underscoring the imperative of always putting the people first and serving them wholeheartedly. On the new journey, it is essential to make solid headway in promoting well-rounded personal development and common prosperity for all, Xi stressed. Noting that Sun devoted his life to the pursuit of truth, Xi stressed the need to learn from Sun's example, advance theoretical exploration and innovation with courage, and continue to write new chapters in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of the times. Xi called on the Chinese people to carry forward Sun's unyielding determination, rise to challenges ahead and break new ground in the country's development. "We must carry forward the fighting spirit, build up our ability, be ready to withstand high winds, choppy waters, and even dangerous storms, and overcome all the risks and challenges we face on the way forward," Xi said. Calling on people to learn from Sun's commitment to unity, Xi also emphasized adhering to the united front and strengthening the great unity among all the sons and daughters of the Chinese nation. Highlighting Sun's global vision, Xi called for vigorously promoting the common values of humanity and actively advancing the building of a community with a shared future for humanity. "Dr. Sun always upheld national unity and ethnic solidarity, and resolutely opposed any word or act attempting to split the country and divide the nation," Xi said. Resolving the Taiwan question and realizing the complete reunification of the motherland is an unwavering historical mission for the CPC, the shared aspiration of all Chinese people, and a natural requirement for the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, Xi stressed. People on both sides of the Taiwan Strait and all Chinese at home and abroad should join hands to oppose the "Taiwan independence" secessionist forces, and work together for the peaceful development of cross-Strait relations and the complete reunification of the motherland, Xi said. "On the basis of adhering to the one-China principle and the 1992 Consensus, we are willing to engage in dialogue and consultations with people of vision and insight from all sectors in Taiwan on matters related to cross-Strait relations and national reunification," Xi said. "We will definitely give full consideration to Taiwan's realities and take full account of the interests and feelings of our compatriots in Taiwan," Xi said. "But we will never leave any room for 'Taiwan independence' separatist activities in any form." "The historical trends are unstoppable. The complete reunification of our motherland must be realized, and it can, without doubt, be realized," Xi said. ■ A gathering commemorating the 160th anniversary of Sun Yat-sen's birth is held at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 12, 2026. Xi Jinping, Li Qiang, Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang and Li Xi attended the gathering here on Thursday.
